wikiGoal: A code wiki for this repository.

pages.title: Data model and ownership boundaries
pages.purpose: Document the Postgres schema owned in supabase/migrations: core tables (profile, exercise, program/program_day/program_slot/program_phase, workout_session, set_log, user_exercise_stat, user_exercise_pin), owner-scoped RLS pattern, additive-migration discipline, and atomic-write RPCs. Explains what is authoritative (set_log) versus derived/rebuildable (user_exercise_stat) and where exercise_swaps/period/body-measurement/coach-decision tables fit.

pages.title: System overview and request path
pages.purpose: Explain the app's layering: framework-free strength engine (src/lib/strength) vs. server-side loaders/actions vs. UI (App Router). Describe the request path for a typical page (server component load -> React cache() memoized clients/catalog -> action mutation -> revalidate), the tab shell (Lift/Track/Program/You), and why choices (batched queries, derived caches like user_exercise_stat) exist.

pages.title: Exercise catalog, variant resolution, and station calibration
pages.purpose: Explain how the merged exercise catalog (seeded templates + user DB rows) forms the Record<id, ExerciseDef> the engine consumes, exercise_id/variant/custom-slug identity rules, station composition (machine/cable/bench/rack/platform profiles, needsStation/needsCalibration), resolveVariant find-or-create semantics, and why machines/cables calibrate against pattern strength on first session while barbell stations do not.

pages.title: Fluid programs: plateau detection and adaptation
pages.purpose: Explain the Fluid (adaptive) program engine: per-movement e1RM plateau detection with hysteresis, the laddered intervention (widen rep range, then ranked-alternative swap), recommend-and-confirm surfacing in-session, and the stall-report.ts contract shared by Fluid, weekly Coach, and monthly review (contiguous per-slot series, deload breaks, patience thresholds). Distinguishes manual swaps (reset plateau state) from coach-generated swap events.

pages.title: Programs, templates, and periodization
pages.purpose: Describe classic vs. fluid program styles, program/day/slot/phase assembly (program.ts), id-preserving upsert/delete-missing builder saves, single-active-program invariant, shared program-templates.ts catalog, and periodization.ts week-specific set/RIR resolution used by classic programs. Covers program routes (/program, /program/[id], edit, new) and the builder's catalog-driven exercise picker.

pages.title: Strength engine: e1RM, coefficients, recommendation, progression
pages.purpose: Document the framework-free src/lib/strength module: the RPE/RIR e1RM model and its inversion, seeded exercise catalog and population strength priors, pattern-strength/Bayesian-shrinkage cross-exercise recommendation, double-progression session targets using bounded exact-exercise history, and the recompute/rebuild contract for user_exercise_stat. States invariants that must be preserved (e.g. do not replace the RPE/RIR model with a bare Epley formula; no continuous recalibration of machine coefficients).

pages.title: UI primitives, design tokens, and copy density
pages.purpose: Document shared UI primitives (Sheet, InfoButton, Button/IconButton, Stepper, Card, Skeleton, Calendar), semantic design tokens, motion/reduced-motion rules, the copy-density rules (labels first, helper text behind InfoButton), the server/client component boundary, and the tab-shell/hideAppChrome conventions for session, recap, planner, and builder routes.

pages.title: Supabase integration: clients, auth, RLS, and RPCs
pages.purpose: Explain how the app talks to Supabase: browser/server client construction with cookie-based SSR, src/proxy.ts calling updateSession() for session refresh (does not gate access), getClaims() as the trusted auth check in layouts/actions, React cache() memoization of createClient/getCatalogMap/getCurrentBodyweight, owner-scoped RLS as the default security model, the sole elevated read path (weekly Coach secret client with mandatory explicit user predicates), and SECURITY INVOKER RPCs for atomic multi-row writes (swap_session_exercise, save_bodyweight_entry, program mutations).

pages.title: Deployment, environment configuration, and release operations
pages.purpose: Cover Vercel/GitHub deployment (main = production, preview branches), required environment variables and which are public vs server-only, migration application via npx supabase db push (tracked, not replayed indiscriminately), the CI workflow (lint, typecheck, Vitest, build, pgTAP RLS suite), release smoke-test checklist, and operational notes (rollback does not undo migrations, token/key rotation procedure).

pages.title: Testing strategy: Vitest, pgTAP, and verification gates
pages.purpose: Describe the two-tier test strategy: co-located Vitest unit/mocked-action tests under src/lib/**/*.test.ts (node environment, pure engine logic plus mocked Supabase action/data-boundary tests), and the SQL pgTAP ownership/atomicity regression suite under supabase/tests/*_rls.sql run against a local Docker Supabase stack via npm run test:db. Documents which supabase/tests scripts are TAP-checked in CI versus manual psql -f checks, and the required verification gate (test, lint, typecheck, build) for application changes.

pages.title: Bodyweight, measurements, and period tracking
pages.purpose: Document the shared weight-calendar Sheet (atomic save/move/replace via save_bodyweight_entry RPC, America/Chicago date handling, current-bodyweight fallback), weight trend windows/goal distance, body measurement tape sites, and the opt-in, privacy-first period tracking feature (consent versioning, calendar bands on charts, no training automation).

pages.title: Coach report, deterministic recommendations, and the planned AI agent
pages.purpose: Explain the versioned CoachCheckInReport contract (Chicago-timezone windows, adherence/duration/set-execution/RIR/hard-set/trend metrics), the deterministic ranked recommendations engine (deload/pain/RIR/plateau guardrails, Do-first/Also tiers), the private read-only weekly Coach API (elevated secret client with explicit user predicates, capability-token auth, no-store/noindex), and the specified-but-unbuilt AI Coach agent's locked decisions and invariants (wraps rather than replaces Coach, tools take the user-scoped client, engine owns numbers).

pages.title: Exercise swap scope and workout planning
pages.purpose: Document the two pre-workout decision flows: the full-page next-workout planner (cookie-persisted, 30-day, device-local choices, no session/history side effects, shared loadNextWorkout with Home/Start) and in-session exercise swap scope (this-workout-only vs remainder-of-program, exercise_swaps JSON on workout_session, SECURITY INVOKER swap_session_exercise RPC). Explains how both interact with fluid adaptation state and manual-swap resets.

pages.title: Track: analytics, exercise review, and monthly progress
pages.purpose: Cover the Track tab's data flows: analytics.ts summaries and board.ts default-compound/pin logic (exact-instance vs family grouping), per-exercise Exercise review (/history/[exerciseId]: Last card, 21-day window, e1RM chart toggle, month-to-month compare, equipment switcher), and the monthly progress dashboard (buildMonthlyReport, workout record replay, exact-window comparisons, shared stall contract consumption).

pages.title: Workout session lifecycle: start, log, rest, finish, records
pages.purpose: Trace the end-to-end active-workout flow: resuming/starting a session with day/week derivation, requireUser/getClaims auth boundary, logging sets and idempotent set writes, the absolute-end-timestamp rest timer surviving tab throttling, session feedback (readiness/pain/note), finishing a session, the paginated PR/e1RM/top-weight record replay (records.ts, workout-records.ts) powering live pills and the cinematic completion recap, and recomputeAndUpsertStat's calibration-anchoring rules.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Orient a coding agent to the lifting-app repository: what it is (Next.js + Supabase progressive-overload tracker with a pure TypeScript strength engine), how the docs map to source, and where to go for each task category. Routes readers into architecture, concepts, workflows, integrations, operations, and testing pages.
